| [NOTE-053](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-053.md) v2 | Consistency Models | Trains a model to map any point on a diffusion trajectory directly to its origin, so one network evaluation generates a sample — FID 3.55 on CIFAR-10 and 6.20 on ImageNet-64 in one step. Trainable either by distilling a diffusion model or from scratch, and the from-scratch mode is what makes it a model family rather than a distillation trick. | Read |
| [NOTE-335](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-335.md) | Self Forcing | Training a few-step autoregressive video model on its own rollouts, with a distribution-matching loss on the whole clip, beats teacher- and diffusion-forced training in matched few-step comparisons (VBench 84.31 against 82.76 and 82.32 chunk-wise), and does not drop when moved to frame-wise generation, where the baselines do. It runs at 17 fps with 0.69s latency on one H100, and its parity with the slower 1.3B base rests on a 14B teacher: the SiD variant, with a 1.3B teacher, scores 84.07 against the base's 84.26. | Read |
| [NOTE-343](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-343.md) v2 | CausVid | Distilling a bidirectional video DiT into a 4-step block-causal student with distribution matching gives a streaming generator: 1.3s to the first frame and 9.4 fps, against 219.2s and 0.6 fps for the teacher. At equal initialization a bidirectional teacher makes a better causal student than a causal one (VBench 94.7 / 64.4 / 30.1 against 91.9 / 61.7 / 28.2). The causal teacher is also the weaker model, so the paper's error-accumulation explanation is not isolated. | Read |
